title: Who really needs a cocktail robot?
slides: Who needs a cocktail robot? Your bartender's next shift?
Bars waste 20% of liquor; robots cut waste to zero.
But the first robot bartender failed—customers hated the wait.
Successful ones mix drinks in 10 seconds, not 90.
Test one pop-up night before buying any machine.
thread_text:
1. Your bartender is wasting money

Bars lose 20% of every bottle to overpours, spills, and freebies. That's pure profit down the drain.

2. The fix: zero waste robots

Automated systems measure every drop, eliminating loss entirely. But early versions had a fatal flaw.

3. The first robot bartender failed

Customers abandoned slow machines. Wait times ballooned to 90 seconds, killing the vibe and the tips.

4. Speed is the secret weapon

Modern robots mix a drink in 10 seconds—faster than a human. That's the difference between novelty and necessity.

5. Test before you invest

Run a one-night pop-up with a rented robot. Measure customer reaction and speed. If it flops, you've lost a night, not a fortune.

instagram.caption:
Your bar is pouring 20% of every bottle straight down the drain.

That’s overpours, spills, and comped drinks eating your margin. A robot measures every drop—zero waste. 🥃

But the first automated bartenders flopped. 90-second wait times chased customers out the door. 💀

Modern systems cut that to 10 seconds—faster than a human. That’s not novelty, that’s a business case. ⏱️

Before you buy, rent one for a single pop-up night. Watch the crowd, time the service. If it fails, you lose one evening.

Would your regulars accept a machine over a human if it meant a faster pour? 🤖
